newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Household firm takes Tunis bourse down by 3.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Household firm takes Tunis bourse down by 3.1 pct.

text.p: The Tunis Stock Exchange index closed down 3.1 percent on Friday, largely driven by household firm Ateliers Mecaniques du Sahel (AMS), which fell by 60.8 percent on its first day's dealing on the computerised system which introduces greater price transparency, bourse sources said.
The 31-share index closed at 485.00 from 500.54 on Thursday.
Volume was 2.28 million dinars against 1.38 million dinars.
AMS dropped by 16.02 dinars to 10.32 dinars. Brokers linked the fall to the introduction of computerised dealing, with its greater price transparency.

Since last October, the Tunis Stock Exchange has been gradually introducing computerised dealing for listed companies, with the system now 24 out of 31 shares. Most of the computerised shares dropped sharply when they made the switch.
Chemical firm ICF, which experienced a similar drop by 46 percent last Tuesday, recovered 1.02 dinar to 35.58 dinars.
UBCI bank, which dropped by 10.44 percent since it was traded on the computerised system, was up 0.7 dinar to 45.2 dinars.
Investment fund SPDIT-SICAF, which dropped by 49.62 percent on Wednesday, was not traded since and remained unchanged at 17.99 dinars.
Banque Nationale Agricole, still traded on the blackboard along with six other banks, was down 0.98 dinar to 31.81.

For its first day on the computerised system, Banque de Tunisie was not traded. Brokers said that generally, trading on newcomers on the computerised system was put on hold because of high gap between ask and bid prices and first settlement comes only two to three weeks later. ($= 1.04 dinar)
